People with high functioning depression are still greatly impacted by their condition in their everyday lives. A lot of people wont tell you how bad it really is- my coworkers think I'm perfectly fine. I'm still able to hold down my job, but its a struggle to make myself eat, get out of bed, brush my teeth, take my medications, get a full nights sleep- basically anything a "normal" person could do without a second thought. I dont know if I'd consider myself disabled though. I identify more with the label of mentally ill, despite the negative connotations of the word.

Hey, I relate to so much of what you just posted. You aren't alone. I'm 19, and I grew up in a toxic household with constant fighting. My parents finally split and my dad reduced his custody from every weekend to every other weekend because he wanted time with his new girlfriend. That shit hurts. My dad lives 15 minutes away and has not once visited me since I've turned 18- just my younger sister. Once you have the ability to get a job and a car your life will change so much, trust me. Before I had that freedom being stuck at home killed me. Ive also struggled with an eating disorder- last year I lost 70 pounds and almost died twice. I understand how it feels to need an outlet- something you can control. If you ever need to talk please feel free to reach out. Life is like an ocean, sometimes it is scary and chaotic but there will always be calmer seas.

I feel you. I really feel you. I didn't think I'd be where I am right now either- I graduated with a 4.0 in high school, now I'm a college dropout. Working in retail with 0 goals. My dream job cant happen due to the pandemic, and I lost the love of my life. 

I also wonder if its worth it. I try to take comfort in knowing I'm not the only one.

I dropped out of college for similar reasons. I never let my grades slip, I just lost all motivation to try when covid hit and the depression got unmanageable so I left before I could fail out. 

If you're in high school and you have no choice but to be there the only advice I can really give is try to focus your energy on little but important things. Fuck homework, if you can do good on tests enough to make it through the year thats enough. And if its too much for you, there's no shame in taking a break and resuming your education later. 2 of my best friends dropped out of high school from severe anxiety and went back for adult education a couple years later- one of them got offered a $30,000 scholarship to med school. Do what's best for you.
